title: Provisioning gate and utilization simulator for dedicated fleet allocations
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Our current dedicated reservation intake focuses on capacity sizing and approvals but lacks a standardized gating mechanism that ties requested throughput guarantees to realistic utilization scenarios and autoscaling guardrails. As a result, proposals sometimes under- or overshoot capacity leading to poor cost efficiency or SLA misses.

Goal: Build a provisioning gate and a lightweight utilization simulator that product managers, sales engineers, and capacity planners can run before final approval. The gate enforces minimal acceptance criteria (throughput profile, burst tolerances, rollback windows) and produces a simulation report showing projected tail latency, expected GPU-hours, and blackout risk under configurable workload traces.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-facing gate (intake form changes + approval checklist), a first-pass simulator prototype (service that consumes historical or synthetic traces and returns capacity recommendations and risk flags), and mapping rules from simulator outputs to autoscaling policy defaults and fleet controls (min/max nodes, preemptible allowance, backfill lanes). Implementation will include: intake schema changes, approval matrix updates, a simulator runnable by SRE/Capacity PMs, dashboard visualization hooks in Console, and rollout plan for pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form includes structured throughput profile fields (qps by percentile, typical sequence length distribution, preferred latency SLO)
Provisioning gate produces a summary report with estimated GPU-hours, expected p95/p99 latency under recommended configuration, and a quantified blackout risk score
Simulator API accepts a historical trace (CSV) or synthetic template and returns a recommended min/max pool size plus autoscale policy suggestion
Approval checklist maps simulator risk score to approval path: auto-approve (low risk), sales-eng review (medium), legal/Security review (high if customer requires on-prem)
Console shows a new per-request simulation card linked to reservation requests in staging environment
Pilot with two internal customers completed and feedback captured
tasks: Design intake schema and new gating fields (PM + Design)
Prototype utilization simulator (SRE/Applied ML): trace ingestion, load model, simple queueing approximation for latency
Define mapping rules from risk bands to autoscale/default fleet controls
Add simulator result card to reservation detail view in Console (frontend + backend)
Document runbook for reviewers with decision criteria and escalation paths
Run pilot with <Customer A> and <internal-staging> and collect telemetry for tuning
comments: 2025-02-11 — Ava: Initial scoping done in sync with Capacity Planning; agreed to prioritize a lightweight simulator that uses queuing approximation rather than full-stack trace replay to reduce engineering cost.

2025-02-18 — Marcus: Spike complete — simulator prototype can approximate p95 latency within ~20% using an M/M/c approximation with observed arrival variances. Needs more tuning for long-tail seq lengths.
2025-02-25 — Leila (Sales Eng): Requested a new field for predictable batch windows (offline processing) so we can suggest cheaper quantization-backed pools for those workloads.
2025-02-27 — Security: Noted that for private/on-prem customers with HSM requirements, the gate must surface a security_review_required flag — added to follow-ups.
2025-03-01 — Marcus: Updated ticket with pilot dates and added Console card mockups link. Moving into Planned for implementation in Cycle 2025-W08.
